title: B.C. RCMP identify twin brothers as Saanich bank shooting suspects
subtitle: The suspects have been identified as two brothers from Duncan, B.C.
article: Twin brothers in their early 20s were responsible for the shooting that injured numerous police officers at a bank in Saanich earlier this week, RCMP alleged Saturday.
RCMP spokesman Cpl. Alex Berube identified the men as 22-year-olds Mathew and Isaac Auchterlonie from the city of Duncan on southern Vancouver Island.
The brothers attended Frances Kelsey Secondary School in Mill Bay, according to a former classmate, who asked Postmedia to remain anonymous.
"Isaac and his brother mostly kept to themselves" during high school hours, the former classmate said. "They never seemed to hang out with anybody else but each other."

A Reddit user shared what appeared to be an Instagram account of one of the brothers, Isaac, describing himself as a "WW2 Pacific War enthusiast."

The now-deleted account features photographs of semi-automatic rifles and ammunition, as well as hashtags in opposition to vaccine mandates and Prime Minister Justin Trudeau. The account also reposted messages from a national gun lobby group, the Canadian Coalition for Firearm Rights.

A video posted on the account shows a letter from the Canadian Firearms Program announcing Ottawa's decision on May 1, 2020, to reclassify a number of firearms as prohibited. On the letter, someone has written the words "keep firearms and don't surrender." The letter is then tossed into a fire.
Six officers were shot and the brothers were killed in the shootout with police on Tuesday outside the Bank of Montreal branch.
Berube said officers have spoken with the twins' relatives, who are co-operating with the investigation.
Investigators are looking into the suspects' backgrounds, and he said neither man had a criminal record or was known to police.

"We understand that the release of the names of the two deceased may answer the who, but there are still many outstanding questions and investigation efforts that need to take place in order to fully understand what took place and why," Berube told a news conference.
"The motive behind the armed robbery and subsequent exchange of gunfire with police has not yet been determined."

Police have also confirmed that the twins are associated with a white four-door 1992 Toyota Camry that has two black racing stripes over the hood and roof, Berube said. The car was found with multiple explosives, which were removed and destroyed last week
Berube said the investigation has so far determined that there were only two suspects in the bank.
"However, we are continuing to look into whether anyone else was involved or associated with the events on Tuesday."
An update on the condition of the injured officers wasn't given.
Earlier, Saanich Chief Const. Dean Duthie had said three of the officers remain in hospital, including one who is in intensive care while another will require more surgeries.
-with files from Sarah Grochowski
